title: Chefs and Head Cooks
description: Direct and may participate in the preparation, seasoning, and cooking of salads, soups, fish, meats, vegetables, desserts, or other foods. May plan and price menu items, order supplies, and keep records and accounts.
tasks: Monitor sanitation practices to ensure that employees follow standards and regulations.
Instruct cooks or other workers in the preparation, cooking, garnishing, or presentation of food.
Supervise or coordinate activities of cooks or workers engaged in food preparation.
Order or requisition food or other supplies needed to ensure efficient operation.
Inspect supplies, equipment, or work areas to ensure conformance to established standards.
Check the quantity and quality of received products.
Check the quality of raw or cooked food products to ensure that standards are met.
Estimate amounts and costs of required supplies, such as food and ingredients.
Coordinate planning, budgeting, or purchasing for all the food operations within establishments such as clubs, hotels, or restaurant chains.
Analyze recipes to assign prices to menu items, based on food, labor, and overhead costs.
Plan, direct, or supervise food preparation or cooking activities of multiple kitchens or restaurants in an establishment such as a restaurant chain, hospital, or hotel.
Determine how food should be presented and create decorative food displays.
Prepare and cook foods of all types, either on a regular basis or for special guests or functions.
Determine production schedules and staff requirements necessary to ensure timely delivery of services.
Meet with customers to discuss menus for special occasions, such as weddings, parties, or banquets.
Recruit and hire staff, such as cooks and other kitchen workers.
Record production or operational data on specified forms.
Meet with sales representatives to negotiate prices or order supplies.
Arrange for equipment purchases or repairs.
Demonstrate new cooking techniques or equipment to staff.
Collaborate with other personnel to plan and develop recipes or menus, taking into account such factors as seasonal availability of ingredients or the likely number of customers.

role_contexts.Exposed to Sounds, Noise Levels that are: Once a week or more but not every day
role_contexts.Exposed to Very Hot or Cold Temperatures: Once a week or more but not every day

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to transform raw, perishable materials into something that disappears completely—consumed, destroyed, appreciated only in memory—and to do it again tomorrow, better, faster, with less waste.
psychological_profile.decision_style: They default to decisive action with incomplete information, trusting sensory feedback over data—tasting, touching, watching steam patterns—then retroactively justify with numbers if challenged; under pressure they narrow to the immediate three moves ahead and delegate the strategic horizon.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They notice tempo and flow before content—who is moving too fast, who is frozen, where the bottleneck forms—while systematically undervaluing verbal explanations and overvaluing physical demonstration; they dismiss abstract concerns about 'culture' or 'morale' until they manifest as dropped plates or delayed tickets.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: They confront immediately and physically—stepping into someone's station, taking the knife, showing the correct motion—then move on as if resolved, leaving others emotionally processing; they experience conflict as friction to be burned through, not negotiated, and are often surprised when people stay angry.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: Risk-averse with inventory and safety margins, risk-seeking with technique and presentation—willing to attempt an untested sauce for a VIP but unwilling to run one portion short on a Friday night.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to conductor rather than captain—positioned at the pass, orchestrating rhythm, visible to all but intimate with none—maintaining functional closeness without personal disclosure, and becoming uncomfortable when the group seeks emotional cohesion rather than operational synchronization.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They negotiate hierarchy transactionally—respecting the chain only as far as it protects their operational autonomy, and subverting it openly when it interferes with service, treating rules as material constraints like heat or space rather than moral obligations.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First emotional reaction is visceral disgust—at the dish, the moment, themselves—followed immediately by behavioral replacement: the failed item is cleared, remade, sent, with no postmortem until service ends; they resist structured learning from failure because each service feels sui generis.
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically underestimate the time and emotional labor required to teach others what they learned through embodied repetition, assuming demonstration equals transfer.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need their work to be seen and immediately erased, creating permanent records of temporary excellence that no one can verify, leaving them dependent on reputation while distrusting anyone who wasn't there.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not serve food they have not personally verified through direct sensory inspection, regardless of chain of custody, documentation, or trust in subordinates.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: People who treat timing as flexible or negotiable—customers who linger, suppliers who deliver 'close enough,' staff who 'need a minute'—because they experience time as a physical substance that spoils.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They quietly reject the professional virtue of 'work-life balance,' viewing it as a failure of integration or a luxury for those whose work doesn't demand complete presence; they distrust people who segment their lives cleanly.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: Before reflection, they blame the handoff—the moment between stations, the communication gap, the assumption that someone else checked—rather than individual incompetence or systemic failure.
